title: Resume-to-JD matcher that explains itself
summary: Rate how well a resume fits a job description, point to the evidence for every match in both texts, and publish the cases where the matcher fails.
context: Candidates and recruiters both want to know why a resume does or does not fit a role, and a bare 73 percent helps nobody. You build a matcher whose every conclusion points at the words that caused it.

You make the data: write or generate at least 8 fictional resumes and 5 fictional job descriptions for invented companies. Pair them so some are clearly good, some clearly bad, and a few fool a keyword matcher (a synonym, a skill used but never named, a keyword in the wrong context).
Hand-label at least 30 pairs before you run anything.
must_have: A matcher that takes one resume and one job description as plain text and returns a fit band (not a falsely precise number), each matched requirement with a quote from the resume and a quote from the job description, and the requirements it found no evidence for.
Your hand labels for the pairs, committed before the first results.
An evaluation script comparing the matcher's bands with your labels, with a confusion table.
A failure-cases section: at least five pairs it gets wrong, each with why, and whether the fix is code, a better method or an honest limit.
A guard that stops the matcher from asserting a skill the resume does not contain, with a test.
nice_to_have: An approach without a model and one with, compared on the same pairs.
The three changes most likely to improve a candidate's match, offered truthfully.
constraints: No paid services, APIs or accounts. A model, if used, runs locally or on a free tier with no card, and its outputs on your committed pairs are recorded so results reproduce without a key.
Fictional people and companies only. Never use a name, gender, age, photo, religion or caste as an input.
The matcher advises; it never rejects anyone.
deliverables: A public repo created after you press Start, with commits spread across the window.
A README with how to run the matcher and the evaluation, your results, what you deliberately ignore, and what is missing.
judge_focus: Whether each explanation can be checked against the two texts.
How hard you tried to break your own matcher, and how honest the failure cases are.
What the matcher must ignore, and how you tested that it does.
A trail of commits: labels first, a baseline measured, then each change justified by a failure.
bengaluru_context: Hiring-tech and talent-platform teams at Bengaluru companies build and defend matchers like this, and an explanation that survives a recruiter's question is worth more than a score.
